chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about a man who had children, so he married two of them and stipulated the dower (sadaq), then he died. From where is the dower calculated: from the total wealth or from their respective shares? He said: From the total wealth. It is in the status of a debt.
ai.seo_question: How is the dower of married children calculated from the father's estate upon his death?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, the Imam clarifies that when a father marries off his children and subsequently dies, the dower (mahr) is treated as a general debt (dayn) payable from the entire estate before inheritance distribution, rather than being deducted solely from the shares of the married children. This distinction ensures that the dower obligation is settled with priority, reflecting the principle that marital debts are liabilities of the deceased's estate rather than mere reductions in specific heirs' portions. This legal nuance highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the precedence of debts over inheritance allocation.
